content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - GPU pool 'g-pool-usw2-spot' saturation detected. queue_growth=+420% last_5m. avg_token_latency increased from 72ms -> 420ms. fallback_capacity insufficient. auto-scaler errors observed. paging oncall: @maria (oncall)

maria (oncall): on it. joining bridge. any immediate customer-impact flags?

raj (sre): seeing queue backlog on worker-side - pods pending due to PodGroup scheduling failures. current queue length 3.2k requests, 95th latency 2.1s. kube events show preemption spikes across spot nodes. logs: `AllocationFailed: insufficient capacity` repeated.

lee (eng-runtime): confirmed: KV cache pressure and batch thrash. runtime saw many model shards evicted when preemptions happened -> warmup thrash. isolation/eviction rate > 30/min.

ana (prodops): @maria routing rules show fallback pools should have filled but on-demand pool at 20% utilization. looks like routing policy rejected due to tag mismatch (spot->ondemand fallback rule failed).

maria (oncall): taking ownership. opening incident bridge: https://meet/redwood/incident/1799998888

sam (customer-success): major voice: customer "atlas-ai" reports spikes in 503s and queued responses for their inference endpoints since ~12:04 UTC. Cx impact: interactive experiences degraded.

raj (sre): pasted autoscaler logs: ```
E 12:03:41 scaler.go:172 allocatePool: failed to request nodes: cloudapi: RateLimitExceeded
W 12:03:45 scaler.go:198 fallbackAttempt: fallback-capacity check failed: reserved_quota=0
```

lee (eng-runtime): quick mitigation ideas: 1) flip routing to force critical customers to dedicated pool, 2) spin up emergency on-demand pool, 3) temporarily lower max_batch_size to reduce KV thrash.

maria (oncall): prioritize options: 1) protect production customers, 2) restore serving pipeline. I will start with forcing critical routing for atlas-ai and beta-pay. @lee please prepare routing change.

lee (eng-runtime): patch ready. command to update routing rule: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing/override \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \ 
  -d '{"route":"/models/atlas/*","pool":"g-pool-usw2-dedicated-1"}'
```

maria (oncall): applied. verifying...

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded for routing override in 2s (rev r-2026-03-15-1799).

sam (customer-success): atlas-ai reporting improvement on their canary endpoint: 200s started returning normal. I'll escalate to their engineering lead and confirm their broader traffic.

jen (infra): trying to create emergency on-demand pool but cloud provider API returns: `QuotaExceeded: GPU quota 0 in region` — looks like our regional on-demand quota exhausted. multi-account quotas are hit.

raj (sre): autoscaler error trace shows backoff to avoid more failed allocation attempts, so it stopped requesting additional nodes. related log: `scaler: giving up after retries - backoff active`.

lee (eng-runtime): we should override autoscaler backoff to force on-demand create. @jen any chance to request quota bump? That takes time. alternative: repurpose a small subset of dedicated pool capacity from non-critical teams.

jen (infra): I can cordon noncritical dedicated nodes and drain low-priority workloads to free ~4 GPUs in 10-15m. will coordinate with infra ops.

maria (oncall): do it. also let's pause spot pool draining to avoid additional churn. @raj can you run the command to disable spot pool eviction controller?

raj (sre): running: ```
kubectl -n infra patch deployment spot-evictor -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
```

raj (sre): done. stopping new eviction waves. will monitor.

lee (eng-runtime): while cordoning, we can reduce max_batch_size and KV cache TTLs to reduce memory pressure: ```
PATCH /v1/runtime/config
{"max_batch_tokens":512,"kv_cache_ttl_sec":60}
```

maria (oncall): applied runtime config tweak. watching effect on 95th latency.

sam (customer-success): atlas-ai confirms reduced 503s on production, still seeing a small backlog on /v1/chat but improved. they're asking for ETA for full recovery.

ana (prodops): creating status page update draft. Suggested text: "Partial degradation for inference API in US-WEST-2 due to capacity exhaustion. Limited subset of customers impacted; mitigation in progress." ask: ok to publish?

maria (oncall): hold until we have stable metrics for 10m.

jen (infra): cordon/drain in progress. freed 4 GPUs by moving batch jobs off. once drained, I'll uncordon bootstrap nodes to accept pods.

raj (sre): manual scale: I'm going to temporarily reduce the autoscaler cooldown to allow one aggressive allocation attempt: ```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap autoscaler --patch '{"data":{"cooldown_sec":"30"}}'
```

deploy-bot: Patch applied to autoscaler configmap (cooldown_sec=30). rolling restart triggered.

lee (eng-runtime): noticed a recent autoscaler rollout (v2.3.1) had a fault in its pool matching logic - could be the tag mismatch mentioned earlier. we should roll back to v2.3.0 if aggressive allocation doesn't land.

raj (sre): allocation request retried at 12:12:31: `AllocateNodes(4) -> success` some on-demand nodes are provisioning.

maria (oncall): good. beginning to see queue drain. queue from 3.2k -> 900 in 8m.

sam (customer-success): atlas-ai confirms near normal performance on 3 of 4 endpoints, they still see occasional spikes.

ana (prodops): status page: published: "Partial degradation resolved for most customers. Some residual latency for high-throughput endpoints; further updates to follow."

lee (eng-runtime): decided: we will roll back autoscaler to v2.3.0 patch. initiating rollback now to eliminate pool-tag regression.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: autoscaler v2.3.0 -> rollout in progress.

jen (infra): on-demand nodes active, routing traffic healthy to dedicated fallback. we still have preemption noise on spot pool but eviction controller paused.

raj (sre): queue now at 180 requests, 95p latency 160ms. steady decline.

maria (oncall): great. next steps: 1) postmortem/drill: what allowed reserved_quota=0? 2) add safety: autoscaler should not backoff when reserved_quota=0 if on-demand(target) available. 3) improve routing policy validation to avoid tag mismatches.

sam (customer-success): I'll follow up with atlas-ai: summary + credits + POC for dedicated lane.

lee (eng-runtime): creating follow-ups: PR to add unit tests for pool tag matching, hotfix to autoscaler to avoid aggressive backoff, and a canary for quota-exhaustion behaviour.

ana (prodops): filing incident ticket and assigning action items.

maria (oncall): thanks all. I'll hand off to oncall-backfill at 13:10 UTC. closing bridge but keeping this thread pinned for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
